beach: Beaches are bright, sandy strips directly adjacent to water bodies, unlike deserts which are vast inland sand expanses without water boundaries, unlike ponds which are small, enclosed dark water bodies, and unlike rivers which are narrow, winding water channels.
bridge: Bridges are narrow, linear structures spanning water channels or valleys, unlike viaducts which are long, multi-span elevated roads crossing land, unlike railway stations which have linear tracks and platforms, and unlike rivers which are natural, winding water bodies.
commercial: Commercial areas consist of dense, large-scale buildings with bright rooftops and adjacent parking lots, unlike residential areas which have smaller, closely packed houses, unlike industrial areas which feature large warehouses and storage yards, and unlike airports which have long runways.

industrial: Industrial areas contain large buildings with prominent roofs and storage yards, unlike railway stations which have linear tracks and platforms, unlike parking lots which are flat asphalt with rows of cars, and unlike commercial areas which have dense bright buildings.
meadow: Meadows are natural or semi-natural grasslands with uniform green textures, unlike farmlands which have organized geometric plots, unlike forests which have dense tree canopies, and unlike parks which have scattered trees and footpaths.
mountain: Mountains are large-scale elevated landforms with rugged topography, shaded slopes, and rocky textures, unlike forests which have dense tree canopies, unlike farmlands which are flat geometric plots, and unlike parks which are flat green spaces.
park: Parks are green areas with scattered trees and irregular footpaths, unlike forests which have dense, continuous tree canopies, unlike commercial areas which are dense building clusters, and unlike farmlands which have organized geometric crop plots.
parking: Parking lots are flat asphalt or paved areas with rows of parked cars, unlike commercial areas which have dense large buildings, unlike airports which have long runways, and unlike industrial areas which have large warehouses and storage yards.
pond: Ponds are small, enclosed water bodies with smooth textures, unlike rivers which are narrow, winding channels, unlike beaches which are sandy strips, and unlike ports which have docks, ships, and containers.
port: Ports are coastal facilities with docks, cranes, and stacked containers, unlike parking lots which are flat car clusters, unlike industrial areas which lack waterfront docks and ships, and unlike ponds which are small, enclosed water bodies.
railwaystation: Railway stations have long, linear tracks and adjacent platforms, unlike airports which have wide runways and terminals, unlike commercial areas which have dense building clusters, and unlike viaducts which are elevated road structures.
residential: Residential areas display dense clusters of small houses with pitched roofs, unlike commercial areas which have large, flat-roofed buildings, unlike industrial areas which feature large warehouses, and unlike parking lots which are flat asphalt with cars.
river: Rivers are natural, winding water channels with reflective surfaces, unlike ponds which are enclosed water bodies, unlike bridges which are linear structures crossing water, and unlike viaducts which are elevated roads.
viaduct: Viaducts are narrow, elevated linear structures spanning valleys or urban areas, unlike bridges which typically span water bodies, unlike railway stations which have tracks and platforms on the ground, and unlike commercial areas which are dense building clusters.
